title: All 2026 Presidents Cup Players Ranked: Complete Performance Breakdown & Scores【SEO】
body:
The United States reclaimed the Presidents Cup on Sunday, overturning a three‑point deficit to defeat the International team 17‑13 at Medinah Country Club. A dramatic finish saw rookie Jacob Bridgeman secure the trophy with a 1‑up win over South Korea’s Min Woo Lee, delivering the Americans their 11th straight Cup victory and capping a weekend of clutch performances from both veterans and newcomers.

From the outset, the competition appeared evenly matched. The International squad entered the final day holding a 9‑8 lead, buoyed by strong showings from seasoned campaigners such as Cameron Smith and Anirban Lahiri. The U.S. side, however, displayed depth across its roster, with several lower‑ranked players stepping up when the pressure intensified. After a modest start on Friday, the Americans surged in the Saturday sessions, narrowing the gap and setting the stage for a decisive Sunday.

Sunday’s fourball and foursomes matches proved pivotal. In the opening fourball, the U.S. pair of Collin Morikawa and Bryson DeChambeau produced a flawless 2‑0 result, erasing the deficit and handing the home team a psychological edge. The International side responded with a narrow 1‑1 split in the second match, but the momentum had shifted. The subsequent foursomes saw the Americans dominate, with a 2‑0 victory by Scottie Scheffler and Patrick Cantlay underscoring their superior teamwork and strategic shot‑making. By the time the singles began, the United States led 13‑11, needing just two more points to clinch the Cup.

The singles matches delivered the drama that defines the Presidents Cup. Early on, several International players, including Louis Oosthuizen and Hideki Matsuyama, secured crucial wins, briefly tightening the scoreline. Yet the Americans’ depth shone through as a wave of first‑time participants delivered key points. Notably, 24‑year‑old Jacob Bridgeman, making his Presidents Cup debut, held his nerve against the world‑ranked 28th Min Woo Lee. The match stretched to the 18th hole, where Bridgeman’s precise iron play forced a short putt that Lee missed, granting the United States the decisive point and sealing a 17‑13 triumph.

Analysts will point to the United States’ strategic selection of players adept in the parkland conditions of Medinah. The course’s firm fairways and fast greens favored players with strong ball‑striking and aggressive putting, attributes exemplified by the American lineup. Moreover, the team’s captain, Zach Johnson, employed a flexible pairing system that maximized chemistry, particularly in the foursomes where communication and complementary skill sets are paramount. The International captain, Trevor Immelman, faced criticism for conservative pairings that failed to capitalize on the individual strengths of his squad, a factor that may influence future selection strategies.

The victory reinforces the United States’ dominance in the biennial event, marking an unprecedented 11‑year streak. While the International contingent showed flashes of brilliance, the gap in depth and adaptability remains evident. For the U.S., the win not only adds another trophy to an already impressive resume but also signals the emergence of a new generation of talent ready to carry the mantle forward. Players like Bridgeman, who delivered under pressure, are poised to become mainstays in future Ryder and Presidents Cup rosters.

Looking ahead, the next Presidents Cup is slated for 2028, with the venue yet to be announced. The International team will likely reevaluate its approach, seeking to blend experience with rising stars capable of thriving on diverse courses. Meanwhile, the United States will aim to maintain its momentum, balancing seasoned veterans with fresh faces to sustain its winning formula. As the sport continues to globalize, the competition promises to grow more intense, and the next edition will test whether the Americans can extend their historic run or finally see the Cup change hands.
